findings.why: 'At the source' implies the lotion changes how the body produces pigment, the same structure/function claim as 'inhibit melanin production', and it sits on the image where most viewers read it. The subline was only partly legible, so confirm the exact wording.
findings.fix: Helps reduce the look of pigmentation

rule_hit_review.why: 'especially those dealing with dark spots' is a third-person description of who the product suits, not a second-person assertion that the viewer has a condition.
'helping inhibit melanin production' claims the product changes a body process (melanin production), which is a structure/function claim for legal review.
'Introducing' signals a new product; it is fine only within 12 months of launch, so confirm the launch date.

tone_read: Calm, declarative and education-first: it names the actives, explains two mechanisms and avoids fear or hype. It sounds like Minimalist.
language_read: The concentration is stated in the brand format (2.5%) and the actives are named precisely, with outcomes mostly hedged ('more even-looking skin tone', 'healthy-looking skin'). The weak point is the mechanism language about inhibiting melanin and targeting pigmentation 'at the source', which goes beyond appearance-scoped claims.
